text:
Alice: Heads up — deploybot blocked RC-124 canary in eu-west-1. Vulnerability scanner flagged a HIGH transitive CVE in libfastcrypto v2.1.2 (image sha256:abcd1234...). Change window closes in ~30m. Options: pin to previous digest, full rollback, regional carveout, or approve with compensating controls. @Carol legal input? @Bob ops timeline?

deploy-bot: [automated] deploybot: scan_flag=HIGH (transitive) — /app/libs/libfastcrypto v2.1.2. Blocked canary: rc-124 (eu-west-1). Evidence: https://scans/reports/1769943210. Action: hold.

Bob: quick question — is this likely an FP? can we fetch SBOM + cosign proof first? If it's only a dev/test transitive dep maybe low runtime risk. Pulling full dependency tree now.

Carol: legal here — we need provenance (SBOM + cosign) before approving a bypass. Without provenance default is to stall. If we can produce signed artifact proof within the window we can consider a scoped exception.

David: SRE note — rollback is fastest (~5m) but causes customer-visible churn. A regional carveout is lower blast radius: we can stop eu-west canary and continue other regions. Pinning to an earlier digest requires rebuild/sign -> ~45m.

Alice: PM prefers avoiding global rollback if possible. Bob — can you run a regional carveout for eu-west-1 and drop canary there? add a note in release notes.

Bob: running command now. Output: ```sh
$ deployctl carveout --region eu-west-1 --release rc-124
> started carveout job id=6789
> canary quota set to 0 in eu-west-1
> updating routing rules... ok
> verification checks passed
```

deploy-bot: [automated] Carveout applied for rc-124: eu-west-1. Canary traffic rerouted to other regions. Gate remains blocked for eu-west-1 until evidence cleared.

Carol: I'm fetching SBOM and cosign metadata from the build repo now. If we produce matching cosign signatures and SBOM provenance within 30m, legal can approve an exception limited to eu-west-1 unpause. Otherwise keep carveout and schedule pin/rollback during next change window.

David: ops action items — enable strict monitoring and an auto-rollback trigger: error_rate > 3% in any region. Add a release-note line about the temporary carveout and fallback behavior for customers. Also notify oncall.

Alice: agreed. Bob, open a release ticket and include rollback playbook + monitoring thresholds. I'll coordinate with compliance once Carol posts evidence. :eyes:

Bob: created ticket RELV-4321. Checklist added: SBOM url, cosign proof, rollback steps, carveout audit log. Pinged @Carol and @Alice. ETA ~25m for docs.

Carol: pulled cosign signature: https://artifacts/reports/rc-124/cosign.txt — verifying signer KMS key now. Signature appears to match build id in SBOM.

Carol: verification complete. Cosign signer key = projects/redwood/keys/signer-ops; build id matches artifact digest. Legal: ready to approve scoped unpause for eu-west-1 with monitoring guardrails.

deploy-bot: [automated] Unblock request received for rc-124 eu-west-1 by Carol. Policy requires 2 approvers. Approval log: Carol (legal) approved. Alice (pm) approved via :thumbsup:.

Alice: Confirming — unpause eu-west-1 canary at 10rps for 30m with auto-rollback on error >1%. Keep close watch and be ready to roll back full release if anomalies appear.

David: monitoring hooks and alerts are in place, oncall notified. Locking the threshold at 1% for this limited unpause. :lock:

Bob: issuing unpause: ```sh
$ deployctl unpause --region eu-west-1 --release rc-124 --rate 10 --monitor-threshold 1%
> resuming canary in eu-west-1 at 10rps
> verification probes started
```

deploy-bot: [automated] Canary resumed in eu-west-1 for rc-124 at 10rps. Gate remains closed for full rollout until final sign-off. Monitoring: dashboards live, alerts configured. :eyes:

Alice: thanks everyone — we'll keep this thread as the single source for rollback/playbook edits. If anything spikes, follow RELV-4321 and escalate to SRE lead.
